behavioral_notes.observation: The module adds a 'certification' value to slide.slide.slide_category and slide_type, gated by a SQL CHECK constraint (_check_survey_id) that a certification slide MUST carry a survey_id->survey.survey, plus a second CHECK (_check_certification_preview) forbidding preview. slide.slide.create() auto-flips any slide given a survey_id to slide_category='certification' and calls _ensure_challenge_category, which retags the survey's certification_badge_id challenge to challenge_category='slides' so the badge surfaces under the eLearning ranks/badges page (reset to 'certification' on unlink). _compute_mark_complete_actions forces can_self_mark_completed/uncompleted=False so a certification slide can NEVER be hand-marked done - completion is earned only by passing the survey. None of this polymorphic content-type linkage or constraint logic is visible in metadata.

Launching a certification builds/reuses a survey.user_input attempt. For a course member with no prior attempt it sudo()._create_answer on the linked survey passing slide_id + slide_partner_id and a fresh invite_token (a new invite_token starts a distinct attempt pool per enrollment); an existing not-done attempt is resumed via its get_start_url(); a non-member gets a throwaway test_entry user_input. The HTTP route /slides_survey/slide/get_certification_url marks the slide viewed (action_set_viewed) then 302-redirects the learner into the survey's /survey/start flow. This attempt-pool bookkeeping spanning slide.slide -> survey.user_input is pure Python.

When a survey.user_input reaches scoring_success=True, slide.slide.partner.survey_scoring_success recomputes True; the _compute_field_value override then writes completed=True on that slide.slide.partner (this is how passing the certification marks the certification slide complete, feeding the channel-level completion/karma chain already in website_slides). _recompute_completion then propagates: for every (partner, channel) whose certification slide now succeeded, it sets slide.channel.partner.survey_certification_success=True, i.e. the attendee becomes 'Certified' for that course. slide.channel.members_certified_count read-groups those flags. This three-hop pass->complete->certify cascade exists only in code.

On create and on state-write, a done user_input with scoring_success=False and a slide_partner_id triggers _check_for_failed_attempt: if the survey reports no attempts left (_has_attempts_left), it emails website_slides_survey.mail_template_user_input_certification_failed and calls slide.channel._remove_membership to drop the learner from the course, forcing a re-enroll before retrying. slide.channel._remove_membership first detaches user_input.slide_partner_id (=False) so prior attempts are preserved but no longer counted against the new pool. This fail-and-evict gating is invisible to metadata.

A survey used as a course certification cannot be deleted (@api.ondelete raises a ValidationError listing the dependent courses). Frontend bridges: /slides_survey/certification/search_read lists certification=True surveys for the upload dialog; create_slide auto-creates a scoring survey (attempts_limit=1, scoring_without_answers, scoring_success_min=70, certification=True, certification mail template) when authoring a new certification; the survey 'finished' and 'retry' controllers thread channel_id/slide_id/slide_partner_id back so the survey result page links to the course; and _get_users_certificates aggregates passed user_inputs onto learner profile and the all-users page (certification_count). These cross-module wirings are code-only.

3 JS files and 3 XML templates, no new OWL components - instead it patches the parent eLearning upload UI (SlideUploadCategory.prototype, SlideUploadDialog.prototype) to add the Certification content category and survey picker, plus a fullscreen course-player script (slides_course_fullscreen_player.js) that drives the embedded certification launch. Assets ride web.assets_frontend (4) and survey.survey_assets (1, result SCSS). This is a thin patch-based frontend not reflected in Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: website_slides_survey (eLearning Course Certifications bridge between website_slides and survey)
software_services: /slides_survey/slide/get_certification_url (launch/resume a certification attempt, redirect to survey)
/slides_survey/certification/search_read (list certification surveys for the upload dialog)
logical_data_erm: slide.slide -> survey.survey (survey_id: the certification behind a slide)
survey.user_input -> slide.slide (slide_id: attempt against a course slide)
survey.user_input -> slide.slide.partner (slide_partner_id: attempt tied to a membership/attempt-pool)
survey.survey -> slide.channel (slide_channel_ids: courses using this certification, computed)
information_flows: side-effect: survey.user_input.scoring_success -> slide.slide.partner.survey_scoring_success -> completed=True -> slide.channel completion/karma chain (parent website_slides)
side-effect: failed last attempt -> certification-failed mail + slide.channel._remove_membership (un-enroll to retry)
side-effect: certification slide -> survey.certification_badge_id challenge retagged challenge_category='slides' (gamification.badge surfaces on ranks/badges page)

capabilities: Gate Course/Slide Completion on Passing a Certification Survey
Enforce Re-enrollment after Failed Certification ('re-purchase' flow)
Award & Surface Certification Badges on eLearning Profiles
Author Certification Content (link or create a scoring survey from the slide editor)
value_streams: Certify-a-Learner: enroll -> launch certification (survey.user_input attempt) -> pass (scoring_success) -> certification slide completed + member marked Certified + badge granted; fail-last-attempt -> notify + un-enroll to retry
Author-a-Certification: create certification slide -> link or auto-create a scoring survey (attempts=1, success>=70%) -> badge challenge retagged to eLearning
policies: 5 record rules + 5 access rules bridging eLearning <-> survey ACLs (no new security groups)
SQL CHECK: a 'certification' slide requires survey_id; a certification slide cannot be set is_preview
certification slides cannot be self-marked complete/uncomplete - completion only via a passed survey
failed last attempt removes course membership (re-enroll required to retry); attempts limited per enrollment via invite_token pools
@api.ondelete blocks deleting a survey still used as a course certification

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_slides_survey is a thin bridge (6 inherited models, 0 new models, 2 routes) that extends its parent value network rather than forming an independent configuration, so it inherits website_slides' Stabell & Fjeldstad 'network' classification: the eLearning platform is mediating infrastructure connecting content/certification providers (officers who author certifications) with consumers (learners), and a credible, badge-backed certification raises the value of platform membership for both sides (community-engagement / network-effect: certificates, badges, leaderboards, learner profiles). This module's specific contribution - gating completion on a passed assessment and issuing a verifiable certification - is an engagement/credentialing service layered on that network, not a sequential transform (not chain) and not a reusable horizontal support engine (the survey module itself is 'support'; here it is consumed by the primary eLearning offering). It is primary because certified course delivery is a core, monetizable line of an eLearning business (the failed-attempt 're-purchase' flow is explicitly framed in-code as letting a user re-purchase a certification). APQC best fit is 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services, matching the parent website_slides: the certification is part of the public-facing eLearning product/demand offering and a conversion/retention lever; the secondary reading is 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital (assess employee competency / corporate L&D credentialing) when the academy is used internally for workforce certification - but the out-of-box surface is the external eLearning website, so 3.0 is primary with 7.x secondary.

standard_capabilities: 'Certification' slide content type linking a course slide to a survey.survey assessment
Completion gating: a certification slide is completed only by passing its survey (scoring_success >= success %)
Attempts-limited certification with per-enrollment attempt pools (invite_token)
Failed-attempt flow: notification email + automatic un-enrollment to allow retry/re-enroll
Certification badges (gamification.badge) surfaced on the eLearning ranks/badges and learner profile pages
Author-time helper that links an existing certification survey or auto-creates a scoring one (attempts=1, >=70%) from the slide upload dialog
typical_fits: Public online academy issuing course completion certificates / diplomas
Internal corporate training with mandatory certification (channel_type='training')
Paid certification courses where a failed candidate re-enrolls to re-attempt
Badge/credential-driven learner engagement out of the box
common_gaps: Expiring / time-bound certifications and renewal workflows (no expiry model out of box)
Verifiable external certificate registry or third-party credential standards (Open Badges export)
Multiple-certification-per-course or weighted final-grade rules beyond single survey pass/fail
Proctoring / anti-cheat beyond survey attempt & time limits
Bespoke certificate PDF layouts beyond the survey module's templates

open_questions: Default auto-created certification thresholds (attempts_limit=1, scoring_success_min=70) are configurable per survey - real tuned values need runtime inspection.
Live counts of issued certifications / certified attendees were not captured (runtime models_with_data = 0).
Whether the 're-purchase after failure' un-enroll flow is paired with website_sale_slides paid courses in a given install is outside this module's code.
Exact karma/badge amounts awarded on certification depend on the linked survey's gamification.badge + challenge config (parent survey + gamification modules).
